title: Assertion with Side Effects (Heisenbug Generator)
pattern: An expression evaluated inside a diagnostic assert block (e.g., `assert!`, `debug_assert!`) modifies state variables, increments counters, or advances iterators.
why_bad: It creates a critical Heisenbug. When assertions are disabled in release/production builds, the side-effecting expression is omitted, altering program execution flow (e.g., skipping elements only in debug builds) and introducing bugs that cannot be reproduced under test.
detection: A mutation, function call with side effects, or iterator advancement appearing within the arguments of a macro containing `assert` or `debug_assert`.
fix: Evaluate the expression outside the assertion, store the result in a temporary variable, and pass the static variable to the assertion.
source: Andrew Hunt & David Hurst Thomas, *The Pragmatic Programmer*, Topic 25 ("Assertions and Side Effects").
